title: Widest Span

story.briefing: The longest cable run in the lattice may not pass through the trunk at all. Find the greatest distance between any two junctions.
story.success: Widest span measured. The cable order goes out.

description: Return the number of connections on the longest path between any two nodes of a binary tree. The path need not pass through the root. A tree with a single node has span 0, and an empty tree has span 0. A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.

examples.explanation: From 1 up through 2 and down to 3 is two connections.

hints: For any single node, the longest path bending at it is the depth of its left subtree plus the depth of its right. The answer is the largest such value anywhere in the tree.
Recomputing a subtree depth for every node repeats enormous amounts of work. One walk can return a depth upward while recording the best span it has seen.
Write a helper returning a node depth. Inside it, compute both child depths, update a running best with their sum, and return one plus the larger of the two.
